summary.headline: MSWIL Q4 FY26 revenue rose ~33% YoY to above INR10,000 crore for FY26, with greenfield plants at ~INR440 crore quarterly and copper pass-through lag compressing margins.
summary.overview: Management said FY26 revenue crossed INR10,000 crore for the first time, with sales up about 33% YoY against a single-digit market. Copper rose about 18% sequentially in Q4, and because pass-through to customers lags by 3 to 6 months, gross margin compressed; management sized the bottom-line lag at about 2% to 2.5%. Greenfield plants (Kharkhoda, Pune, Navagam) generated over INR400 crore in Q4 but remain under ramp-up, with Pune at roughly 40% to 50% utilisation. Management guided FY27 capex to about INR200 crore and reiterated the company is debt-free.

financial_highlights.value: Crossed INR10,000 crore for the first time
INR443 crore (as cited by analyst; management said over INR400 crore)
~INR127 crore (as cited by analyst, not confirmed by management)

segments.name: Greenfield plants (Kharkhoda, Pune, Navagam)
segments.commentary: Kharkhoda is at about 80% utilisation and running to plan, Navagam at about 60% with one model ramping, and Pune at about 40% to 50% as forecast volumes have not come through. Management guided greenfield volumes to ramp over about 1.5 quarters for Navagam and a couple of quarters for profitability parity.

segments.name: Existing plants
segments.commentary: Running at around 80% capacity utilisation, which management said triggers capacity expansion backed by firm customer orders.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex guided at about INR200 crore, mix of greenfield for already announced customer expansions, automation/digitisation, and replacement capex.
Copper-related pass-through lag expected to be recovered in Q1 FY27 volumes under contract terms; management would not predict copper prices.
Greenfield profitability expected to reach parity with existing plants over a few quarters once volumes ramp; no plant-level margin guidance given.
Management said order wins continue across ICE, EV and hybrid and expected Q1 FY27 growth to continue.
Management expects the greenfield annualised revenue run-rate of about INR2,000 crore to INR2,100 crore (set earlier for all plants combined) to be achieved; Pune volume ramp timing unclear.
capex_capacity: Existing plants at ~80% utilisation; expansion triggered only on firm customer orders.
Kharkhoda ~80%, Navagam ~60%, Pune ~40% to 50% utilisation across the three greenfield plants.
FY26 capex about INR190 crore; FY27 capex guided at about INR200 crore.
Management said it will not build plants without firm orders in hand.
demand_pricing: Management says the company is winning business across ICE, EV and hybrid powertrains.
Company supplies 9 of the top 10 passenger vehicle programmes (per slide referenced on call).
Copper pass-through: majority of customers on a 3-month lag, a few on 6 months; JPY-related pass-through also applies on a similar lag.
Polymer (PVC/petchem) prices rising; management said it will work with customers jointly, with no quantified impact given.
Some OEM model ramp-ups have been delayed or volumes below forecast, particularly in Pune; management said the models have launched and in some regions volumes lag.

qa_highlights.question: Will current revenue fully reflect the sharp copper increase seen to Q4, and how will margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 largely reflects prior-quarter copper prices, with the Q4 increase flowing through in Q1. Cost recovery is full with a lag, but a denominator effect causes a marginal EBITDA dip. Full-year margins are not as pronounced as the Q4 dip.

qa_highlights.question: How much copper and currency impact is embedded in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Sequential copper rise of ~18%, adding ~2% to sales. Copper is 24% to 28% of COGS. Bottom-line effect from lag estimated at 2% to 2.5%. Currency impact is marginal and JPY-linked, with pass-through in the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: At what greenfield run rate do margins match existing plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a run-rate or plant-level margin guidance. It said margins will reach parity once volumes ramp, which will take a few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR2,000 crore greenfield revenue target still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR2,000 crore to INR2,100 crore was an earlier combined expectation for all plants, not plant-specific, and that Q4 greenfield revenue of over INR400 crore shows volumes are growing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature and size of FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximately INR200 crore, similar to FY26, split across greenfield for announced customer expansions, automation and digitisation, and replacement capex.

qa_highlights.question: Will ramp-up costs and manpower growth normalise in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said newer greenfield plants will need a repeat of the manpower front-loading, while brownfield execution is faster. It expects FY27 sales growth to absorb the cost growth; no quantified outlook given.

risks_watch: Copper and polymer price volatility; pass-through lag of 3 to 6 months keeps near-term margins under pressure.
Greenfield ramp-up delays, especially Pune at ~40% to 50% utilisation, and customer launch delays.
Manpower cost growth of roughly 25% in FY26 ahead of FY27 volume ramp.
Customer concentration; management stated no customer, country or component should exceed a set share of sales, without disclosing the figure.
Management declined to share plant-level margin, pass-through detail, or customer programme details, limiting analyst visibility.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand and order wins, but defensive and reticent on margin and plant-level detail, repeatedly declining to quantify greenfield profitability or copper pass-through mechanics.
